subject: marathon runners
one_liner: Video meetings with a 26.2-mile minimum. Your calendar finally reflects your commitment.
brand_voice_notes: Distance is a meeting duration. Breathlessness is stakeholder input. Treat unnecessary endurance as a procurement requirement. Dry, specific, straight-faced; never explain the joke.

hero.h1: This meeting could have been a marathon.
hero.sub: Split is video conferencing for marathon runners. AI turns heavy breathing into meeting minutes, breakout rooms sort by pace, and the call ends at 26.2 miles. Please plan your other calls accordingly.

features.title: Minutes from your lungs.
features.blurb: Our AI transcribes every gasp into a decision. Two sharp exhales count as budget approval. A long silence assigns the action item to whoever is still moving.

features.title: Break out by pace.
features.blurb: Nobody at 7:30 per mile should have to hear a 10:00-per-mile opinion. Split moves attendees into pace rooms before those differences become audible.

features.title: The finish line is mandatory.
features.blurb: The host can end the meeting once everyone logs 26.2 miles. Dropped connections rejoin at the same mile. We have closed the obvious loophole.

pricing_tiers.name: Just Listening
perks: One excuse to skip a scheduled long call per billing cycle. Once joined, all 26.2 miles are due.

pricing_tiers.name: Negative Split
pricing_tiers.tagline: For teams with a time to beat.
perks: AI assigns decisions to your breathing

pricing_tiers.name: Race Director
perks: Procurement deck with a foil blanket

testimonials.quote: We approved the annual budget at mile 19. Nobody remembers the figure, but the transcript says unanimous.
testimonials.name: Mara Ellis

testimonials.quote: My old meetings ran over. Now they run exactly 26.2 miles. I appreciate a defined scope.

testimonials.quote: I tried to leave at mile 22. Split referred me to the commitment I made during onboarding.

demo_screen_concept: One active video meeting, Sunday long call. Three runner camera tiles show Mara, Dev and Colin with distance, pace and microphone state. A pace-room selector filters attendees. A right-hand AI minutes panel interprets breaths as corporate approvals; its transcript changes as the user advances the meeting one mile at a time. A full-width distance strip shows the slowest runner at mile 18.2 of 26.2. Controls mute the local microphone, turn the local camera off, toggle captions, request a gel, advance a mile, and attempt to end the call. Muting records Mara’s new microphone input as muted and produces no new decisions from it; earlier notes and other runners’ updates remain intact. Ending is blocked with an explicit inline distance explanation until all attendees reach the finish, then a completed meeting view offers a restart. All data and controls are a local simulation.

design_direction.style: Dark sports-broadcast minimalism. OLED-black canvas, oversized condensed headlines and elapsed-distance numerals, chartreuse timing strips, precise white divider rules. Restrained photographic video tiles provide the only texture.
design_direction.archetype: Video-First Hero from the bundled landing library, adapted as a static broadcast still: giant type beside an active call frame, distance strip, open feature rows, runner quotations and a membership comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 180ms control colour feedback and small opacity transitions on camera state. No ambient loops. Reduced motion disables transitions and smooth scrolling.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Large asymmetrical two-column hero with a three-line condensed statement at left and wide runner photograph inside a call frame at right. Meeting duration and distance are HTML outside the photograph. A lime full-width distance ruler closes the hero. Lower sections use open ruled rows, dark portrait strips and joined pricing columns. Mobile stacks copy before photograph.
design_direction.design_review: Retained the bundled OLED dark style and Video-First Hero composition. Replaced its light navy palette with custom black and timing lime, and its generic Inter pairing with library Bold Statement. Read the latest seven concepts; no style/palette/font tuple matches. Frontend-design review: retained lime because it functions as the distance and timing colour of a running broadcast; removed decorative feature numbering because the features are not a sequence. One large photographic call frame carries the hero.

images.rationale: Hero: one editorial runner photograph anchors the broadcast call frame. Demo: two additional runner portraits plus the hero reused for three camera tiles. Testimonials: reuse those same named runners as participant headshots; no additional generation is needed. Three distinct images, four successful generation calls including the corrective hero retry, within the existing daily cap.

items.prompt: Editorial sports photograph, candid and deadpan: one female marathon runner in her late thirties with short brown hair wearing a completely plain charcoal technical running shirt and small wireless earbuds, jogging alone on an empty park path at dawn, looking toward a camera slightly ahead at chest height as though attending a very serious work video call. Single focal person on right half with open path on left. CORRECTIVE FEEDBACK: previous shot contained a white letter-like clothing mark near the shorts. Frame CHEST UP ONLY, crop above waist, show NO shorts, all clothing totally unbranded with absolutely no symbols or lettering. Natural human proportions, realistic perspiration, cool restrained colour grading, deep asphalt green-black #10120F shadows, subtle lime #D3F55A clothing seam, soft grey daylight, documentary sports broadcast still, no artificial cinematic glow. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
items.judge_verdict: Pass on attempt 2. First attempt rejected for a small logo-like clothing mark; chest-up retry removes it. Correct subject, realistic anatomy, restrained dawn palette, no text or logos visible.
